newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday December 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday December 9.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Anti-graft hero and former Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro slammed an investigation against him as "a joke and a squalid vendetta". Finance police raided Di Pietro's homes on Friday to search for clues of alleged irregularities he committed during his Tangentopoli (Bribesville) inquiry (all).

* Documents in a police report leaked to the press allege that banker Pierfrancesco Pacini Battaglia (recently jailed on corruption charges) avoided jail in 1994 thanks to Di Pietro's protection (Corriere della Sera).
* Leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema said he did not believe the accusations against Di Pietro (all).

* The government criticised Giorgio Fossa, head of industrial association Confindustria, for making scathing remarks against the centre-left administration. Fossa had said Prime Minister Romano Prodi government's days were numbered if it did not do more to help business. The government, Fossa said, should make it easier for private business to create jobs but instead "it raises taxes and therefore does not understand the reality of the country" (all).
* In an interview Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani says "Fossa does not look well (at economic data). In the last six months this country has changed" (La Repubblica).
* In an interview Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti says "Maybe Fossa exaggerated a bit, but in the substance he is right...This 1997 budget is strongly unbalanced on the side of taxes" (La Repubblica).
* In a visit to India Foreign Trade Minister Augusto Fantozzi sponsored business agreements worth some 1.5 trillion lire involving Fiat, Pirelli, Stet, Ansaldo and other companies (La Stampa).
